newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon $2.5 bln debt deal may grow-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon $2.5 bln debt deal may grow-dealers.

text.p: Raytheon Co's highly anticipated $2.5 billion debt offering expected to come later this week may be increased in size, dealers said on Tuesday.
"We're hearing that the deal may be upped in size and that additional tranches may be added to meet demand," said one dealer.
"We hope to get the deal done by close of business on Thursday," said Raytheon spokesman Robert McWade.
When asked about the possibility of the deal getting increeased in size, McWade said, "No comment."

The rating agency said the ratings reflected the $2.95 billion debt-financed acquisition of Texas Instruments Inc's defense unit and the pending $9.5 billion debt- and equity- financed purchase of Hughes Electronics Corp's defense operations.

S&P said the two transactions are expected to constrain financial flexibility materially for an extended period and cautioned if Raytheon failed to make adequate progress in regaining credit protection measures appropriate for BBB credit quality, ratings could be lowered.

Raytheon, headquartered in Lexington, Massachusetts, is an international high technology company operating in several businesses - commercial and defense electronics, engineering and construction, aircraft and major appliances.
((-- Nancy Leinfuss, U.S corporate bond unit, 212-859-1675))
